title: The Tea-Pot
summary: The porcelain teapot was proud of her delicate spout, her curved handle, and her noble task of brewing fragrant tea for the grand parlor....
full_text:
The porcelain teapot was proud of her delicate spout, her curved handle, and her noble task of brewing fragrant tea for the grand parlor.

One afternoon, the maid dropped her on the stone hearth; the handle broke off, and she was cast into the courtyard dustbin.

A poor woman found the cracked teapot, filled it with black earth, and planted a flowering hyacinth bulb in its center!

The bulb took root, sprouted fresh green leaves, and bloomed into exquisite, fragrant blossoms! The teapot felt a new, profound joy: "I no longer serve the vanity of tables; I hold living life in my breast! To nurture a living flower is infinitely greater than pouring tea!"
moral: When pride is broken, a higher purpose of nurturing living life begins.
